good_sentence: It was the dog that barked all night.
bad_sentence: Was it the dog that barked all night.
notes: The cleft keeps 'it' before 'was'; inverting them turns the focusing statement into a yes-no question.

good_sentence: It was John who solved the puzzle.
bad_sentence: It John was who solved the puzzle.
notes: The copula must follow 'it' directly; placing the focus 'John' before 'was' breaks the cleft frame.

good_sentence: It is the manager who makes that call.
bad_sentence: It is the manager makes that call.
notes: The cleft requires the relativizer 'who' to open the focus clause; dropping it leaves an ungrammatical run-on.

good_sentence: It was Mary that I saw at the station.
bad_sentence: It was Mary I saw that at the station.
notes: The relativizer 'that' must immediately follow the fronted focus; burying it inside the clause is ungrammatical.

good_sentence: It was in Paris that they first met.
bad_sentence: Was it in Paris that they first met.
notes: Fronting 'was' ahead of 'it' converts the cleft assertion into a question rather than focusing the locative.
